To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Weber fractions for contour-curvature discriminations are viewpoint-invariant if and only if they are based on the attributes sag, area, or mean-deviation.

the Weber fraction for curvature discrimination depends on the particular attribute of the contour used as the cue, and that the attribute that gives the smallest Weber fraction is the maximum deviation (sag) of the contour from a straight line.
Weber fractions for the discrimination of curved shapes are viewpoint-invariant for sag, area, mean-deviation, and, to a lesser extent, for arc-length, but not for the other attributes.

a fundamental issue of perceptual organization: What are the invariant cues for the visual discrimination (and hence the perceptual organization) of curved contours?
